note: What must land before what. The orchestrator reads this to decide which work is unblocked; nothing here is a preference, each edge is a hard technical dependency with the reason stated.

waves.name: Reconnaissance
waves.exit: Registry, gap report, dependency graph, ownership and risk register exist and regenerate cleanly.

waves.name: Foundation
waves.exit: Primitives, server + schema + RLS, auth and authz, test harness — all stable and merged.

waves.name: Product
waves.exit: Every domain capability implemented against real endpoints.

waves.name: Hardening
waves.exit: Sweeps current with W2 — starts as soon as any capability is reviewable, not after the last one.

waves.name: Integration
waves.exit: Full regression green; no regression carried forward.

waves.name: Certification
waves.exit: Every gate passes; certification report generated from the registry.

edges.why: Route tables, route tests, coverage and the release gates are generated from it. Building screens first means hand-maintaining hundreds of route checks.
23 CTAs are inert today. Without a modal there is nowhere for a form to live, so no CRUD can be built.
PublicShell, PortalShell and KioskShell do not exist. Portal screens have no chrome to render inside.
Real data, persistence, audit and server-side authorization are DoD clauses. No screen can be certified before this exists.
Portals are separate audiences with their own sessions; they cannot be built against a session model that does not exist.
Contract tests assert both sides import one Zod schema. Without the package there is nothing to assert against.
A job card references a customer and a vehicle. The Mini ERP chain cannot start from records that do not persist.
An invoice is raised from a completed job card; the business invariant forbids invoicing without one.
Parts are reserved before repair and consumed during it. Without stock movements the chain has a hole in the middle.
Report aggregates must come from the API over the ledger, not client arithmetic over one page of rows.
BarList and Donut are trapped inside accounting/Reports.tsx; every other chart screen would otherwise copy them.

edges.to: AppointmentCalendar, CRMCalendar, Workshop Calendar, Staff Scheduling
edges.why: Four screens need one calendar. Building it four times is how the duplicate-component rule gets broken.
One scaffold — header, meta, tabs, related records, timeline, activity rail, audit — reused rather than nine variants.
Deliberately last among product work: the kit already renders these, so they are the safest work to defer and the easiest to parallelise.
Mobile is a DoD clause on every screen; certification cannot run against unverified layouts.
A failing critical golden path is an absolute release blocker regardless of any score.
A backup that has never been restored is not a verified backup.

contention.app/src/routes/index.tsx: Every product agent adds routes here. Once the registry drives the route table this stops being a contention point — which is why G1 comes first.
contention.app/src/data/repository.ts: Agent 05 owns it; product agents consume it. Changes are requested, not made.
contention.app/src/data/generated/ar.ts: Agent 19 owns translations; product agents supply English keys and request the Arabic.
